Commentary.Commentary: However, the hosts have set a big target of 335, courtesy their first innings lead of 205. It certainly would be difficult on this track to chase down. In this series so far, they have bowled out Bangladesh thrice and will be backing themselves to get the better of them again. Do the Bangla Tigers have it in them to fight fire with fire? Let's find out on the other side of the break.

A brilliant bowling performance from Bangladesh has given them a glimmer of hope. They hardly took any time to clean the tail up as Shakib finished with a 6-wicket haul. Mehidy Hasan also chipped in with a couple of wickets towards the fag end. The skipper was on fire since morning and troubled the batsmen constantly with his variations. There was a handy 33-run partnership between Hetmyer and Chase which meant that Windies go past 300 but once Taijul Islam broke the stand, there was no substantial contribution down the order.
OUT! That's the final nail in the coffin! Coming in with the arm, Gabriel clears his front leg to play an agricultural slog but misses and the ball hits the stumps. WINDIES ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 129!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Safe! Coming in with the arm, Gabriel tries to defend it but seems to have got an inside edge onto his pads. An appeal for an LBW is turned down. Shakib takes the review but the replay confirms that there was a nick.
Shakib feels he has trapped Gabriel in front of the stumps and goes for the DRS straightaway.
Slow through the air, Gabriel lunges in defense.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! Timber! Shakib Al Hasan gets a 5-fer, his 18th in Tests. He has been outstanding throughout and deserves every bit of it. Floated outside off, goes straight on after pitching. Cummins leans ahead to block it but misses the line to see the furniture behind him get shattered. However, the umpire tells the batsman to wait and refers it upstairs to check whether he was bowled or the keeper disturbed the bails. The replays confirm that the ball hit the wickets.
Turning in from outside off, Dowrich clears his front leg to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Nicely done! Slow through the air outside off, Dowrich times his drive through covers and gets a brace.
Dowrich is right forward to that one and defends it calmly.
Spinning in from outside off, Dowrich goes for an expansive drive but gets beaten. He needs to take his chances as he is batting with the tail.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Hangs back and punches this one out.
A shout for an LBW turned down! Spinning in appreciably as Cummins prods forward to defend but seems to have got an inside edge onto his pads. That might have saved him.
Spinning in to Cummins as he turns it to mid-wicket.
Leans ahead to this one and blocks this one right under his eyes.
Floated delivery, takes the outer half of the bat to roll towards covers for a run.
Quicker one on middle and leg, tucked to short fine leg for a run.
The ball hits the batsman low on the pads. They pick up a single. The Umpire signals a leg bye.

OUT! Smart bowling from Mehidy has brought another wicket for him. He spots Holder coming down the track and hence, bowls a straighter one outside off which is quicker in pace. The Windies skipper plays for the turn but gets beaten comprehensively. Nurul Hasan behind the wickets is lightning quick to take the bails off. Miguel Cummins walks out to bat next.
Bye! Spinning down the leg side as Shane misses his flick. Nurul fails to gather it as well as the ball rolls towards fine leg. A run taken.
Beaten! Quicker one outside off, Dowrich leans ahead to block it but the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Loopy ball around off, swept nicely to the man at square leg.
Similar ball, worked with the spin to short mid-wicket this time.
Slow delivery which turns in, Shane hangs back in defense.
Flatter on off, Holder goes back and keeps it out.
Slower through the air on the leg stump. Holder tries to defend but misses to get hit on the pads.
On the stumps, kept out.
Fires this down the leg side, maybe he was anticipating the batsman to come down the track. Holder does not do so and lets it through.
Nicely played! He leans into the delivery and strokes it to the man at covers.
Floats it up on off, Holder defends it uppishly but wide of the man at silly point.

Howzat? Seems to be safe. Straighter one outside off, skids through after pitching. Dowrich tries to defend it but looks like he has missed it. Nurul Hasan takes it and along with his mates appeals loudly. However, the umpire stays put. No review taken as well. The replay shows why as there was no bat involved.
Straying on the pads, turned to square leg for a run.
Floated around off, kept out watchfully.
Fullish ball on middle and leg, tucked with a closed bat face to mid-wicket.

OUT!  Bowled 'em! A poor shot selection has led to his downfall. Tossed up ball around off, skids on after pitching. Chase goes too far across and plays all around it. He tries to sweep it but misses it completely to get cleaned up. Jubilation for Mehidy Hasan!
Jason Holder strides out to bat.
Fullish ball outside off, stays low. Chase goes deep in the crease to  counter it.
Mehidy Hasan is back on.
A bit quicker in pace, spinning away. Roston lets it go.
Stump-to-stump line, kept out watchfully.
A little more air on this one, Roston goes at it with hard hands but gets it off the inner half back towards the bowler.
Fullish this time on middle, Chase taps it towards mid on.
On a flatter trajectory, spinning away, placed through point for a run.
On middle and leg, tucked around the corner for a single.
Floated well outside off, eased through cover-point for a run. 8 from the over.
Shorter in length, punched off the back foot to covers.
SIX! All the way! Chase gets another tossed up delivery on middle. He lofts it over the long on fence for a biggie.
A low full toss on the pads, Dowrich flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
On the stumps, defended.
Full on the pads, worked to mid-wicket.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end.
On the stumps, kept out.
Fires it on middle, Dowrich strokes it down to long on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gives it air on off, it is driven to mid off.
Flighted ball outside off, Dowrich waits for it and guides it through third man for a couple.
Starts off with a tossed up delivery on middle, Dowrich drives it to mid on.

We are back for the afternoon session. Out come the players and they are followed by Roston Chase and Shane Dowrich who will continue their innings. Shakib Al Hasan will start the proceedings after Lunch. Here we go...
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

With only 4 wickets left, will the Windies go all out after the break? How many more will they want to add or will the Bangladesh bowlers bowl them out? All these questions will be answered in the afternoon session. Join us for it in a while.

This session - 27 overs, 89 runs and 5 wickets. This session has belonged to the visitors but the Windies, courtesy their big lead are way ahead in the game. Wickets is what Bangladesh needed when the day began and that is what they got. Shakib ran through the middle order as he now has 4 to his name. Just as when it looked like the hosts would be bundled out in this session, Hetmyer and Chase stitched a handy stand and took the lead above 300. The former did perish to Abu Jayed but Windies would feel they still have a lead which should be enough.
Full on middle, it is eased to mid on. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Length again outside off, Chase need not play at those.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Poor ball and it has been put away! Short and wide outside off, Chase gets on top of the bounce and cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Good length on off, guided towards point.
The keeper is upto the stumps.
Good length delivery on off, Chase defends it out.
Slow through the air, played with soft hands to mid on.
Full on leg stump, Chase pushes it back to Shakib who tries to deflect it onto the stumps but misses. A run is conceded.
Floated ball on middle and leg, played with soft hands to mid on.
This one stays low and is going down the leg side, Chase crouches and tucks it to deep backward square leg for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up ball, Chase leans ahead and blocks it towards covers.
Another ball which is way outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
FOUR! Nice way to get off the mark! Full and outside off, Dowrich leans into it and strokes it through covers. The ball beats the diving fielder and crosses the fence.
Once again too wide outside off, the batsman need not play at it. Poor this from the pacer. He should be making the new batsman play.
Full and wide outside off, Dowrich lets it be.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! The bowling change works wonders. A partnership which was starting to build has been broken. Abu Jayed bowls another inswinger from outside off, Hetmyer tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Windies lead by 302. Shane Dowrich is the next man in.

A huge appeal but not given! On a length outside off, this one shapes back in. The batsman tries to defend but the ball brushes his pads and goes towards the keeper who dives to his left and takes it. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. The impact was outside off.
Abu Jayed is back on.
Goes for the sweep but mistimes it towards square leg.
On middle, Chase works it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Shorter in length on middle, Chase pushes it back to the bowler.
Fullish ball on middle, defended solidly off the front foot.
Slow through the air, kept out watchfully.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on.
Hangs back to this one and plays it towards covers.
Outside off, Shimron tries to cut this one but only manages a bottom edge.
Punches it down to long off for a run.
Goes for the sweep but is beaten by the away turn.
Quicker on middle, Chase keeps it out.
Flatter on off, the batsman pushes it back to the bowler.
FOUR! The boundary brings up the 300-run lead for the Windies. This is down the leg side. Hetmyer works it fine and fetches himself a boundary.
Plays the paddle sweep through fine leg for a run.
The off spinner on middle, Chase tries to work it with the turn but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball lobs towards short leg who takes it. The players appeal but the umpire is not interested.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The arm ball on middle, Hetmyer tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Slower through the air on off, Hetmyer with the turn guides it to point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This one stays low after pitching outside off, Chase guides it to point.
On the stumps, the batsman lunges and keeps it out.
Flighted ball on off, Chase drives it to covers.
On the pads, Hetmyer tucks it around the corner for a run.
Fires it on middle, this one skids through. Chase is a little late in bringing his bat down. The ball takes the inside edge and goes towards square leg for a run.
The straighter one on the pads, Hetmyer tries to defend but gets an inside edge through backward square leg for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the stumps, the batsman pushes it to covers.
Quicker outside off, the batsman tries to cut but chops it to point.
Fires it on the pads, SH tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
FOUR! Once again Hasan's first ball has been put away for a boundary. Hetmyer uses his feet and slams it through mid on and the ball races away.
On the stumps, defended.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. Two runs added to the total.
Floats it up on off, kept out.

In the air... but Abu Jayed seems to have lost it. Chase tries to go downtown but only manages to hit it high in the air. Abu Jayed from mid on turns and runs after it but then pulls out of the catch. The ball lands just ahead of him and Mehidy Hasan from mid off does the mopping up job. 2 taken by the batsmen.
Goes for the sweep shot but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball goes to the fielder at silly point who hits the bull's eye at the keeper's end but the batsman is well in.
Flatter on the stumps, Chase keeps it out off the back foot.
Comes over the wicket and bowls it on the pads, Chase tries to defend but gets it off the inner half through square leg for a run.
Flighted ball on off, driven to mid off.
A half-tracker outside off, SH pushes it through covers and gets to the other end.
Flighted ball on off, Hetmyer tries to drive but gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Tucks it around the corner for a quick run.
Flatter on off, Chase pushes it back to the bowler.
Shorter in length outside off, Hetmyer tries to cut but the ball gets big on him. He does well to play it with soft hands and onto the ground.
Gives it air on the stumps, the batsman keeps it out.
Fires it on the stumps, the batsman pushes it towards mid on for a run.
Flighted ball on off, defended.
Pushes it through the off side for a run.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Loopy ball on the stumps, Chase lunges and defends it onto the ground.
A little too full on middle, Chase goes for the big hit but finds the man at mid on.
On the stumps, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
Slower through the air on off, Chase first thinks of leaving it but at the very last moment gets his bat down and guides it to point.
Flighted ball on middle, Chase swing hard but mistimes it to mid on.
Floats it up on off, Hetmyer guides it towards point for a quick run.
On the stumps, Chase defends it onto the ground.
FOUR! Swept and swept fine! Goes down on one knee and sweeps it against the spin. Connects well and fetches himself a boundary.
BEATEN! Excellent delivery! Pitches it on off and then gets it to turn away sharply. Chase tries to defend with a stride forward but gets beaten.
Shorter in length, cut through point for a single.
Floated outside off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Spinning in sharply, defended off the inner half of the bat towards short leg.
Floated up on middle, the batsman eases it to mid on.
Chase tries to go inside out over covers but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket and takes a couple.
Flighted ball on middle, kept out.

Has that been dropped? Not sure! Shakib bowls the arm ball on middle, Chase tries to defend but gets an inside edge which looks like it hit the boot on the full. The ball lobs towards the short leg fielder who is not alert. He tries to catch it but does not.
Slaps this through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Hetmyer works it to short leg.
Time for Drinks!

OUT! The bowling change does the trick for the tourists! Bangladesh are up and running this morning, as their spinners have picked up 4 wickets for only 45 runs. Islam tosses it up from around the wicket. The ball comes in with the arm but Hope plays for the turn and hence, misses to get hit right in front. Taijul appeals vociferously and up goes the umpire's finger. Shai asks his partner whether he should take the review. The reply to that is no. Looked quite dead to the naked eye as well. The visitors will aim to chip away at the wickets.
Tight channel! Around off, spinning away a touch. Hope shoulders arms to it.
Well played! Fractionally short, enough for Hope to camp back and cut it through covers. A couple taken.
Outside off, spinning away, left alone.
Islam gives this one a lot of air, Hope plays it with soft hands towards covers.
Fullish delivery, eased off the front foot to mid off.
Taijul Islam comes on for a bowl.
Spinning in sharply, defended towards short leg.
Slow through the air, Shimron lunges in defense.
Leans ahead and taps it towards mid on for a run.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total. Hetmyer is off the mark.
On the shorter side, kept out watchfully.
Shimron Hetmyer comes out to bat.

OUT! Plumb! A review goes down the drain for the Windies. Shakib is on fire as he picks his third of the morning and fourth overall in the innings. Tossed up ball on a fullish length around off, Powell instead of coming forward opts to camp back and defend it but misses to get hit on the pads. The visitors appeal in unison and the umpire obliges. Hetmyer has a look of anguish on his face and walks gingerly towards his partner. After a discussion, he signals for the 'T' finally. Time for the replays. Snicko doesn't dectect anything. The Hawk Eye rolls in and shows three reds. He was living dangerously and he has finally perished. Another failure for him. The Windies are ahead by 265 runs.
Powell has been trapped in front of the stumps, but after giving it a long hard thought, he opts for the DRS. Seems like a goner though.
Powell skips down the track and jams it out to mid on for a single.
Coming in with the arm, tucked with a closed bat face through mid-wicket for a run.
Comes right forward to that one and dead-bats it.
Slow through the air outside off, eased to covers to rotate strike.

FOUR! He is taking his chances and they are coming off at the moment. He does have a liscence to go for his shots as his side is way ahead in the game. Tossed up ball well outside off, Powell comes down the track and drives it away from his body through covers. The connection is good and a boundary results.
Quick in pace and shorter in length, spinning in sharply. Powell rocks back and cuts it to cover-point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shai Hope comes out to bat.

OUT! It is on the line! Now we know why the keeper was so confident. Good work by him once again. His second stumping today. Keemo Paul tries to repeat the feat he did on the last delivery. This time though he dances down the track a little. He misses and the keeper quickly dislodges the bails off. He appeals and the umpire goes upstairs. Replays roll in and it shows the boot is on the line. The third umpire first by mistake, flashes not out on the board but then corrects it to OUT. Third for Shakib and his second today. The skipper leading from the front but he needs support from the other end.
Another stumping appeal against Keemo Paul has been referred upstairs. Once again the keeper is very confident.
SIX! Keemo Paul has nailed that! He shows he is no mug with the bat. He goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence. The 50 is up for the Windies and the lead now is 258.
Loopy ball on middle, Paul strides forward and blocks it.
Slower through the air on off, defended.
Floated up on off, this one pitches and turns. Beats the outside edge of the batsman who lunges to defend.
An appeal for an LBW denied! Coming in with the arm, Powell tries to block it but is hit above the knee roll. Mehidy appeals but the umpire turns it down. Might be going down leg.

Uses his feet once again in an attempt to unsettle the bowler but he is on the money. Powell defends it off the inner half in the end. It is a bit uppish but falls safely to the right side of the short leg fielder.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A touch shorter, spinning away, Powell goes for the cut but misses.
Strides ahead to the loopy ball and keeps it out.
Powell uses his feet once again and drags the heave through wide mid on. A couple taken.
Slow through the air outside off, Powell places it towards point for a run.
Tries to sweep this one but gets hit on the pads.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.

Ooh! Almost dragged that back! Spinning in sharply from outside off, Powell misreads the length as he tries to guide it to third man. An inside edge is induced and luckily for him, the ball hits his pads and not the stumps.
Comes ahead confidently and buries this one into the ground.
Spinning into Powell who turns it to mid-wicket.
Tucked with a closed bat face to the same region.
Fuller in length, played off the inner half through mid-wicket for a run.
Kieran uses his feet again and tries to block it but the ball hits his pads and rolls towards covers. Hasan appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Came way down on this occasion.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! Shot! Slow through the air on middle, Powell comes down the track and lofts it down the ground. The timing is not that good as the fielder at long off is interested for a while. However, it clears him with ease and also the fence.
Loopy delivery, Powell lunges in defense.
Tossed up ball, defended solidly off the front foot.
Paul leans ahead and defends this one off the outer half towards the same region.
Floated well outside off, placed towards point.
Coming in with the arm, Paul blocks it solidly.
Leg Bye! Spinning in from outside off, Powell comes down the track and tries to defend it but the ball lobs off his pads towards covers. The batsmen take a run.
Tossed up delivery, kept out watchfully.
A bit of halt in play. Keemo Paul gets his thigh pad in place.
Turning in slowly from around off, Keemo lunges in defense.
Powell is nimble on his feet and this time he is well-balanced. Powers it towards long off for a run.
Uses his feet and goes for the heave. He does not connect well as the ball goes off the inner half towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
Gives it air on off, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Floats it up on off, this one turns into the batsman. He tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
FOUR! Welcome into the attack Mehidy! Paul goes down on one knee and sweeps it over square leg. Connects well and it goes for a one-bounce boundary through backward square leg.
Tossed up generously, Keemo taps it through mid off for a run. A successful over for Shakib.
On a flatter trajectory, defended from the comfort of the crease.
Spinning past the outside edge of Paul as Nurul takes the bails off again but this time the batsman is safe.
Tossed up ball, clipped through mid-wicket for a run.

Not Out! No bat involved. Bangladesh lose a review. Tossed up delivery on off, spinning in. Powell skips down the track to play it down the ground but seems to have missed it. The ball goes off something, deflects off the keeper's gloves and settles into the hands of first slip. The visitors appeal but the umpire stays put. Shakib opts for the review after taking a glance at the keeper. Well, the Snicko shows clear daylight between bat and ball. The third umpire also checks for the LBW. Hawk Eye shows that the ball is missing the leg stump. It is to be mentioned that the keeper missed a stumping chance as well but by no means, it was an easy one. Not easy to collect deflections cleanly.
Have Bangladesh got another? An appeal for a caught behind has been turned down against Powell. They have gone for the review.
Kieran Powell strides out to bat.

OUT! Brilliant glovework from Nurul Hasan! Tossed up outside off, goes straight on after pitching. Smith plays for the non-existent turn and gets beaten. The keeper is lightning quick to take the bails off. The players appeal and the square leg umpire takes it upstairs. Time for the replays. They show that Smith has taken his back foot out of the crease as he has overbalanced himself. The question is has he been able to drag his foot back in when the bails are off? From the side view angle, it is seen that Devon's back foot is in the air while the bails come off. Good start for Bangladesh this morning.
Another appeal for a stumping has been taken upstairs. The man in question is Smith this time. The keeper seems more confident on this occasion.
Well bowled! Jayed goes wider of the crease and angles in a length ball sharply. Paul is up to it as he tucks it towards mid-wicket. A maiden for Jayed.
Slightly overpitched, drive towards point where the fielder dives to his right to stop it.
Length ball on the fifth stump channel, Keemo shuffles across and lets it go.
A play and a miss again! Similar delivery, drawing Paul into a drive and the ball once again whizzes past the outside edge of his bat.
Hurled wide outside off, Paul goes after it but gets beaten.
Keemo Paul is having a issue with his legs. He was running gingerly between the wickets and seems to be a little uncomfortable.
Back of a length ball outside off, Smith places it through point to rotate strike.

Safe! Quick reaction from Paul saves him. Loopy ball outside off, spinning away. Keemo skips down the track in order to tonk it down the ground but misses. Nurul Hasan takes the bails off but the batsman turns back and seems to have put his bat inside the crease. The square leg umpire refers it upstairs. The replays confirm that the right-hander is safe.
There is a referral for a stumping against Keemo Paul. Seems that he was successful in getting his bat back in the crease .
Shorter in length, kept out watchfully.
Half-tracker from Shakib. Smith help-pulls it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Straighter one from Shakib, Devon puts his head down and defends it calmly.
A loosener! Down the leg side, Smith tickles it past the keeper. Mehidy runs after it and keeps it down to a couple.
Good use of the feet from Keemo Paul and he gets his first run in Test cricket! Strokes it through wide mid off to rotate strike.
Shakib Al Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Short of a length around off, defended solidly off the back foot. 4 from the first over of the day.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! This is one of the areas where Smith scores a lot. Short and room on offer, Devon pounces on it and cuts it through point to pick up a boundary.
Closer to the off stump but not close enough to make the batsman play.
Pretty harmless ball, way outside off, the southpaw doesn't fiddle with it.
Back of a length ball outside off and it moves away after landing. Devon chases it a bit and plays it with an angled bat towards point.
Starts off from around the wicket and bowls a length ball in the tight off stump corridor. Smith covers the line and defends it stoutly.

We are set to get rolling. The players and the umpires make their way to the middle. Devon Smith and Keemo Paul to resume their innings. It will be Abu Jayed to bowl first up this morning. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the surface says that the cracks have opened up quite a bit. Adds that they are quite deep and as a result, there is variable bounce. Mentions that it did play a role in Mahmudullah's dismissal as the ball stayed low. Ends by saying that it will be difficult for the batsmen.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 3. The Windies are in pole position at the moment and will be aiming to remain on top. With a healthy lead of 224 and a lot of batting to come, they can take their time and tire the opposition out. Bangladesh, on the other hand, need to be proactive and play with a lot of intensity. You never know, on a two-paced surface, if you get a few wickets, that can cause a collapse. Expect another absorbing day of Test cricket.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Bangladesh on the other hand, started well with the ball this morning and have finished well today. They have got 1 but need another 9 and they need them quickly. The wicket is a two-paced one and Shakib will hope their bowlers can come to the fore and keep the Windies down to a total which can be chased. Join us for all the action on Day 3 at 1000 Local (1500 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye.

The Windies though are still way ahead in the game courtesy their bowlers who gave them a massive lead by bowling the visitors out cheaply. They would now want their batters to capitalize on this and set a huge target for the away side.

So, Bangladesh have gotten a wicket before Stumps and it is their captain who provides it to them. Their pacers were off the radar in the few overs they bowled. Brathwaite and Smith looked at ease and just as it seemed that they would end the day unscathed, Shakib struck of his very first ball.
Paul negotiates the last ball well! This is floated up on off, the batsman lunges and keeps it out. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Full on off, driven back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on middle, kept out.
Flighted ball on off, Paul defends it onto the ground.
Keemo Paul, the nightwatchman, makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! KABOOM! Shakib brings himself on and strikes off his very first ball! The slider from him on off, this one also stays low and skids through. Brathwaite fails to get his bat down in time. The ball brushes the pads and hits the off stump. An early wicket for Bangladesh and it is of the centurion of the first innings. He walks back cheaply. Can Bangladesh get another before Stumps?
Shakib Al Hasan to roll his arm over now.
Fuller in length outside off, it has been stroked to the man at covers.
On a length around off, Smith defends it onto the ground.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Length again on off, the batsman pushes it to mid off.
Back of a length on off, it is pushed to the fielder at covers.
Wide outside off, left alone.
On a length around off, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
Works it with the angle towards mid-wicket for a run.
A bumper on middle, Brathwaite ducks under it.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They manage to come back for the second.
Fuller in length on middle, KB strokes it to mid on.
Shortish on off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
Good length again outside off, comes back in after pitching. Still not enough for the batsman to play at it.
NO BALL! The bowler has oversteped! Outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
Length again outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Shortish outside off, the batsman cuts it to point.
Length ball a little too straight. Kraigg whips it through mid-wicket for a run.
Kamrul Hasan is into the attack.
Wider outside off, Smith shoulders arms to it. A maiden but by no means a threatening one.
Another length ball outside off, the batsman makes the third leave of the over.
Length on off, Smith pushes it back to the bowler.
Fuller in length outside off, the batsman makes another leave.
Wide outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
On a length around off, Smith mistimes it to mid on.
Brathwaite prods forward and defends this one with the spin.
Spinning in sharply to go past Brathwaite's defense and ping him high on the pads. Mehidy puts in a chirp appeal but the umpire stays put. Might have been going down leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Slower through the air, defended solidly off the front foot.
Spinning into Kraigg as he tucks it to the mid-wicket region.
Tossed up ball on middle, Brathwaite hangs back and defends it towards short leg.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

A huge appeal but the umpire shakes his head! An inswinger by Jayed. Pitches around middle and off and then comes back in. Brathwaite tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal follows but the umpire is unmoved. Good call by him as Hawk Eye later on shows it would have gone over.
Fuller in length on off, KB defends it onto the ground.
On a length outside off, left alone.
On a length around off, kept out.
Loopy ball on off, kept out. So a good comeback by the bowler after going for 8 on the first two balls.
Fires it on the pads, Smith misses the flick to get hit on the pads. A stifled appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head.
Flatter on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Better from Hasan. He tosses this up on off, the batsman keeps it out.
FOUR! This time he serves a half-tracker. Devon Smith once again has no qualms in putting it away as he whips it through mid-wicket. Consecutive boundaries.
FOUR! A gift first up! A loopy full toss on middle, Smith duly accepts it. He flicks it through mid-wicket and gets off the mark in style.
Mehidy Hasan to bowl from the other end.
On the shorter side on middle, Brathwaite works it to square leg. End of a poor first over by Jayed.
KB is off the mark! Slightly shorter outside off, he guides it through covers for a couple.
Slightly short outside off, Brathwaite goes for the pull but is beaten by the low bounce.
Shortish and on the body of the batsman. Kraigg works it to leg gully.
Wide! You do not see a lot of that in a Test match. This is way outside off and the umpire stretches his arms. The keeper dives in front of first slip and stops it.
Full and outside off, Kraigg lets it be.
On middle, Brathwaite works it to mid-wicket.
No ball! A false start by the bowler. Down the leg side. The batsman lets it be and the keeper does well to make a diving stop. Jayed has overstepped.
